body:
Measured 14 Nov 2026 with the app's own [perf] spans (emulator, build 151, against VM 108; six library artists opened twice, BACK between). Shell (the page frame) draws in 51 to 132 ms every time. "full" (the discography) on the FIRST visit: 1069, 1209, 817, 994, 818 ms; one artist (2SICH) never reached "full" (the catalogue does not know the name); on the SECOND visit: 159, 293, 242, 249, 221 ms. So an artist page waits about a second cold and a fifth of a second warm; the owner's 1.5 to 2 s on the A35 fits a slower first round trip, it is not a stall in drawing.
CAUSE FOUND IN THE CODE (not a bug in one place, a structure): ArtistScreen waits for libraryArtistCatalogueProvider (catalogue_providers.dart:156), which on every visit (autoDispose) (1) searches the catalogue for the artist's NAME, (2) when several artists share the name asks up to three artists' releases together to pick the one that overlaps the library, and only then (3) catalogueArtistReleasesProvider asks the releases again by id and (4) does one database look-up per release. Two or three round trips in a row to the server (and from it to Deezer), repeated on every visit; the warm time is the HTTP layer's cache, not a remembered answer.
FIX AT THE SOURCE (proposal, for the advisor): remember which catalogue artist a library artist IS (a column on the phone's artist row, or better the server's answer in the artist feed: P2-12, "artist pages come from your own server": one call that returns the identity, the popular songs and the releases, cached on the server), so the page asks once by id and a repeat visit asks nothing. Until P2-12: persist the matched catalogue id per library artist on the phone (survives restarts) and start the releases request in parallel with the name search when the id is known. Not done yet; N-14 stays todo with this as its plan.
